title: Join a flat-pack shelf flush to an upright cabinet side on two cam bolts and lock both eccentric cams tight
instruction: Join the flat-pack shelf flush to the upright cabinet side on its two cam bolts with both cam locks turned tight using the stubby screwdrivers, then put both screwdrivers back in their cradles and move both hands clear.
context: The difficulty is the constrained assembly order and a simultaneous 0.5 mm-play alignment. Both recessed 15 mm cam housings start 90 degrees closed across the shelf's 8.0 mm edge bores, stopping the upright's 7.0 mm bolts 8.5 mm short if pushed first. One hand must steady the loose 28 cm shelf while the other engages a stubby Pozidriv screwdriver at least 1.5 mm into each cam slot to open both throats, then both hands must slide the shelf square so both 7.0 mm bolt heads enter the 8.0 mm bores simultaneously while both open cams wait undisturbed, before turning each eccentric cam 180 degrees in turn to draw the seam flush and lock it. Anyone who has assembled a flat-pack bookcase or kitchen cabinet recognises this joint and the page-one mistake of leaving a cam turned across its bore so the shelf refuses to seat.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left, z up from the bench). Fixed layout; nothing varies by seed. Upright cabinet side: white 16 mm melamine-faced particleboard (EN 312 P2), 32.0 cm wide x 14.0 cm tall, inner mating face at x = 36.0, centred on y = 0, clamped square to the bench at its back by two steel L-brackets at y = +-13.0. Screwed into Ø 5.0 mm holes at y = +11.0 and -11.0, z = 7.2, two Häfele Minifix S100 steel connecting bolts (art. 262.27.029, 24 mm drilling distance, Ø 7.0 mm head) project 2.50 cm toward -x (bolt tips at x = 33.5). Assembly support block: dark-grey smooth HDPE riser 6.4 cm tall, fixed on the bench, 26.0 cm wide over x = 26.5..36.0 (under both cams) and 15.0 cm wide over x = 17.5..26.5 (leaving 6.5 cm of each rear shelf wing overhanging 6.4 cm above the bench for finger grasps). Shelf: oak-decor 16 mm melamine particleboard, 14.0 x 28.0 x 1.6 cm (406 g plus two 10 g cams), resting level on the support block (mid-plane z = 7.2) with its joining +x edge on yellow start ticks at x = 31.8 (4.2 cm from the upright, within +-2 mm and +-2 deg). Drilled along y = +-11.0: two Ø 8.0 mm horizontal edge bores (centreline A = 8.0 mm) meeting two Ø 15.0 mm x 12.5 mm-deep top-face cam bores 2.4 cm from the +x edge, holding two Häfele Minifix 15 zinc housings (art. 262.26.033) turned +90 deg clockwise from open (red top arrows pointing -y, blocking the bores). Two 5.4 x 5.4 x 2.9 cm blue-grey HDPE cradles with Ø 15.0 mm funnelled vertical wells sit at x = 28.5, y = +24.5 and -24.5 (yawed 45 deg), each holding a Wera 355 PZ Stubby screwdriver (PZ 2 x 25 mm, art. 05008854001, 79 mm long, 37 g) tip-down and upright. Both arms start at ready.
scoring: 0 permanently if at any step the shelf's mid-plane drops below z = 5.6 cm (off the support block) or either screwdriver falls to the bench with its handle centre below z = 3.2 cm (on a real bench, judged from the trial video). Otherwise scored at the end of the trial. Seam gaps are the horizontal +x openings between the shelf's joining edge and the upright face at y = +11.0 and -11.0 cm; every nonzero level requires both seam gaps >= -1.0 mm, shelf lateral offset <= 2.0 mm (the 7 mm heads in the 8.0 mm bores hold it within 0.5 mm), and shelf tilt <= 3.0 degrees. A cam is locked when turned into [150, 195] degrees clockwise from open (+x) and clamping its bolt head against pull-off (>= 5.0 N in simulation; on the bench, red arrow within 30 degrees of -x and seam opening <= 0.5 mm under a 10 N -x luggage-scale pull). 0.25: shelf aligned and pushed onto both bolts with both seam gaps <= 2.5 mm (the cams' draw: the bolt heads inside the cam pockets, not a lateral allowance). 0.50: seated so (both seam gaps <= 2.5 mm) and at least one cam locked. 1.00: both seam gaps <= 0.6 mm, both cams locked, both stubby screwdrivers standing upright in their cradles (tip within 12 mm horizontally of the well centre, <= 20 mm above the bench, within 15 degrees of vertical), and every part of both hands >= 30 mm clear of the shelf, cams, and screwdrivers, held for 1.0 s (20 steps) with <= 1.0 mm shelf drift. Bench tools: 150 mm steel rule, 2.5 mm and 0.6 mm feeler leaves, phone inclinometer, 10 N luggage scale, overhead photo, and trial video.
reset_notes: Between trials (about 30 seconds): lift each stubby screwdriver, engage each cam lock and turn 180 degrees counter-clockwise back to open (0 degrees, red arrow pointing +x toward the upright); slide the shelf straight back along the HDPE support block until its +x joining edge rests on the yellow start ticks at x = 31.8 cm (4.2 cm from the upright, within +-2 mm and +-2 degrees); turn both cam locks 90 degrees clockwise to their closed start pose (+90 degrees, red arrows pointing -y); stand both stubby screwdrivers tip-down in their cradle wells at x = 28.5, y = +-24.5 cm; inspect chipboard bore mouths for burrs.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz PhysX, 20 Hz control. Shelf 8.0 mm edge bores are 16-stave rings around 7.0 mm bolt heads (0.50 mm radial play). Closed cam skirts stop bolt entry 8.5 mm short; compliant eccentric spiral flanges pull the seam flush and lock over 150-195 deg CW. Driver-to-cam coupling applies equal-and-opposite axial torque only while pressed >= 1.5 N at >= 1.5 mm slot depth, with zero lateral or tilt support so released stubbies topple. Wood splintering and bolt threading are unmodeled.
